title: Readiness Heuristics Cheat Sheet — Dedicated Deploys
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational-first cheat sheet for product ops and oncall engineers prepping or validating a Dedicated deployment rollout. This is intentionally terse — heuristics, quick thresholds, and immediate actions to reduce runway friction.

Context notes (quick):
- This lives alongside the dedicated deployment README and the go/no-go checklist but focuses on signal heuristics and fast mitigations (not the full gating flow).
- Target audience: Release PM, SRE oncall, Dedicated account AE, solutions engineer.
- Typical release profile: 0–5% canary for 24–48h, then 5–25% over 48–72h, then incremental expansion. Heuristics below assume baseline capacity already validated in staging.

Quick metrics to watch (always spike-alert if any crosses):
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 (token gen time and end-to-end). Thresholds: p95 > 250ms over baseline -> investigate. p99 > 600ms -> throttle expansion.
- Error rate: 5xx / rate limit rejections. If 5xx > 0.3% sustained for 5m -> run incident triage.
- Cost per 1k tokens (observed): if 10%+ delta vs estimate -> hold and debug quantization / routing changes.
- Throughput: concurrent requests / GPU utilization. If GPU util < 30% during steady load -> check batching heuristics, autoscale config.
- KV cache hit ratio: < 60% on repeat-y workloads -> tune prefix masking or cache TTL.
- Autoscaler thrash events: more than 2 scale-in/out cycles in 10m -> consider raising cool-downs.

Heuristics (fast rules of thumb):
- Canary window: minimum 24 hours with real traffic; extend to 72 hours for embeddings-heavy or long-context workloads.
- After a p95 regression of >20% vs baseline, revert to prior model variant instead of patching mid-canary.
- For Dedicated, prefer conservative burst capacity (20%) rather than aggressive autoscaling during initial 7 days.
- If cost forecast overshoots >15% of commit, enable cheap fallback model variant and reduce batch sizes incrementally.
- For latency-sensitive routes, keep batch-window <= 20ms and prefer single-request priority lane.

Rollout knobs (what to tweak, in priority order):
1) Traffic ramp slope: lower slope by half if p95 increases >10% in any 30-minute block.
2) Model variant routing: enable model fallback path at 0.5% traffic immediately if errors appear.
3) Batch size distribution: shift 10–25% of traffic to smaller batch-queued workers for <100ms targets.
4) KV cache TTL and prefix grouping: increase TTL for high-repeat prompt sets first.
5) Autoscale cool-down: set to 180–300s during ramp to avoid oscillation.

Incident triage quick playbook (first 15 minutes):
- Step 0: Post summary to #prod-ops-rollouts channel, tag release PM + oncall.
- Step 1: Check errors/latency dashboard and trace samples (p99 tail). Identify whether errors are model-timeouts, infra OOMs, or gateway-level rejects.
- Step 2: If p99 latency or 5xx spike, immediately reduce inbound traffic by 50% via traffic-router (canary gate).
- Step 3: If errors are model-level (OOM/hang), route 100% of canary to last-known-good model variant and pause rollout.
- Step 4: If infra capacity (GPU saturated but model healthy), enable burst capacity (if provisioned) or scale up reserved nodes; if not possible, roll back to previous capacity config.
- Step 5: Open incident note in tracker (link), capture top 3 trace ids and a brief timeline.

Acceptance quick-check (pre-traffic):
- Config parity: runtime flags, quantization profile, and autoscaler settings match staging snapshot.
- Test prompts: run the 12-key sanity set (see linked artifacts) to validate latency and output shape.
- Cost smoke: run a 30-min synthetic probe at expected QPS to validate cost model (<10% variance).
- Security: KMS keys rotating? network policies allow customer CIDR only.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal alert (slack): "Canary 7% -> p95 latency +18% vs baseline. Holding traffic. Investigating traces. @oncall @release-pm"
- Customer-facing status (AE to customer): "We observed a latency increase during early traffic ramp. We have paused further expansion and are validating a fix — ETA 2h. No data exposure. Will update in 30m."

Lightweight KPI map (owner + fast thresholds):
- p95 latency: owner = eng-sre, threshold = baseline +10% (action: hold).
- 5xx rate: owner = serving-runtime, threshold = 0.3% sustained 5m (action: reduce traffic).
- Token unit cost delta: owner = product-ops, threshold = +10% vs estimate (action: enable fallback variant).
- Cache hit ratio: owner = applied-ml, threshold = <60% (action: reconfigure TTL).
- Autoscaler cycles: owner = infra, threshold = >2 cycles/10m (action: increase cooldown).

Open questions / risks to note (quick):
- How will enterprise customers verify isolation of telemetry while we collect in the early canary? (action: AE to confirm telemetry scoping)
- Long-context models tend to OOM silently — do we have safe memory caps per-slot? If not, add a per-job OOM detector.
- Ops fatigue: repeated small thrashes are high-cost. For first 7D after launch, prefer human-in-the-loop approvals for scale decisions above 30%.

Triage snippets (copy-paste checklist for slack or runbook):
- "Checkpoints: p95, p99, 5xx, GPU util, KV hits. If any cross thresholds -> reduce traffic 50% and escalate to oncall."
- "If rollback: route traffic to model:vX or enable-fallback-route; run 12 sanity prompts and verify p95 within 10% of baseline before re-opening ramp."

Appendix: 12 sanity prompts (short descriptions)
- Short completion (avg 12 tokens) -> validate cold-start latency.
- Multi-turn chat (4 turns) -> validate KV cache effectiveness.
- Large-context concat (2k tokens) -> memory sanity.
- Embedding batch of 50 items -> embedding throughput and latency.
- Reranking micro-batch -> correctness/time slice.
- Function-calling stub -> structured output shape.
- etc. (full list in linked PRD)

Notes to self (todo):
- Convert this cheat sheet into a 1-page printable quicksheet for oncall.
- Add a small dashboard tile that shows the 5 fast thresholds (p95, p99, 5xx, GPU util, cache hit) in one line.
- Verify the AE communications template with legal for regulated customers.

End — quick reference.

(Informal — expect edits; this is a working distillation of patterns we've seen across three dedicated beta launches.)
